hook_text: A metre is 100 centimetres. So a square metre is 100 square centimetres? Wrong by a factor of one hundred.
clip_script: One metre is 100 centimetres. Everyone knows that. Now draw a square one metre on each side and fill it with little one-centimetre squares. Along the bottom: 100 squares. How many rows? 100. So one square metre is 100 times 100, which is 10 000 square centimetres, not 100. Now a cube, one metre each way. 100 along, 100 across, 100 up: a million cubic centimetres. That is why a cubic metre holds 1 000 litres, because 1 000 cubic centimetres make a litre. So a rainwater tank of about 2.12 cubic metres holds about 2 120 litres, enough for two weeks at 150 litres a day. The rule: the conversion factor is used once for every direction. Twice for area, three times for volume. And the safest trick of all: change every length into one unit first, then multiply.
visual_style: A one-metre square fills with a grid of tiny squares, a counter racing to 10 000; a cube fills in layers to a million; the cube becomes a water tank with a litre gauge rising to about 2 120.
pacing: Quick hook, steady grid count, a big beat on 10 000 and a million, a confident rule to finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for surface area and volume of prisms and cylinders, and capacity in litres.
